transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-04-01
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Acme PM), Tom Alvarez (Acme Platform Eng), Sara Kim (Acme ML Eng)

Auto-generated Summary (optional):
- Weekly POC sync focused on integrating Redwood SDK for function/tool calling and producing structured output for Acme's product catalog assistant.
- Discussed current integration blockers: SDK usage patterns, authentication (KMS / key rotation), VPC egress rules, and latency/cost tradeoffs.
- Agreed next steps: share prompts, run benchmark, provide SDK snippets, and review security docs.

Topics:
- SDK function-calling patterns (TypeScript/Python examples)
- Structured output schema (JSON schema for product attributes)
- Latency vs cost: hosted vs dedicated vs fallback routing
- Security: SOC2, KMS, VPC, audit logs
- Integration artifacts: demo app, benchmark sheet, decks

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: ok, uh thanks everyone for joining, we, we have about an hour. quick check, do I have everyone?
[00:07] Priya: yes hi this is Priya, thanks Maya.
[00:09] Tom: Tom here.
[00:11] Sara: Sara, hi.
[00:12] Liam: Liam from Redwood, hey all.

[00:30] Maya: Great. Agenda  quick status, go over the integration notes from last week, review the benchmark plan, look at the SDK function calling patterns and then action items. Sound okay?
[00:38] Priya: Sounds good. main thing for us is making sure the structured output maps to our product catalog, and that the function calls can trigger downstream inventory lookups without leaking PII.

[01:05] Liam: yeah, and to add, we did a patch on the SDK so function calls can return a typed JSON block and Redwood will validate the schema server-side if you pass the schema in the request. note: that validation is currently an opt-in flag in the Python SDK. (laughs)

[01:30] Sara: oh nice. is that the new Type infer thing?
[01:33] Liam: no, it's simpler  you hand over a JSON schema and the response is validated and if it fails we'll supply the raw text + the closest JSON we could parse. there's a small mismtach risk when the model hallucinating fields.

[02:05] Tom: That raises a question  we need strong audit logs for these validations; are the validation failures included in the audit trace?
[02:12] Maya: yes, we log request/response IDs, schema validation result, and any fallback. all of that is in the per-request trace and shows up in the Console as an event. we can include that in the security docs.

[02:45] Priya: Great. Just to re-state our constraints: production latency target is <= 250ms p50 for single-turn product attribute requests, and cost needs to be sub $0.004 per request on average. that's kind of our sweet spot.

[03:05] Liam: Okay that's useful. One note  for 250ms p50 you'll likely need dedicated capacity or a very aggressive caching strategy (prefix / KV cahce). if you can tolerate slightly higher p50 and rely on caching we can reduce cost.

[03:45] Tom: can you explain the caching options again? we saw docs but want the recommended config for our workload  many short queries, high QPS during sales peak.

[03:53] Liam: sure. two levers: prefix caching (for repeated prompts) and KV cache for model KV keys during generation for multi-turn. for single-turn attribute extraction, prefix caching with a small TTL works well. Redwood Optimize can propose TTLs based on your request distribution; we'll run a suggested profile in the benchmark.

[04:25] Priya: do you support cache invalidation from our side? like if we update product metadata, can we purge keys?

[04:30] Maya: yes, we have purge APIs in the Dedicated offering and an admin endpoint for hosted. we'll send the API reference link.

[05:00] Sara: switching to authentication: we plan to use our internal KMS for encrypting keys  do you support customer-managed keys?

[05:07] Maya: yes, Redwood Private + Dedicated support CMK via KMS/HSM. Hosted supports envelope encryption and can integrate with customer KMS through a dedicated contract; we'll surface the exact integration plan in the security doc.

[05:45] Speaker 1: (background) sorry the build is, yeah..

[06:00] Liam: On SDK examples  here's the plan: provide both a TS and Python minimal example showing function definition, call, and structured output parsing. We'll include error handling for schema validation failures and an example of fallback to plain text.

[06:30] Priya: can you show a quick snippet live? even pseudocode is fine.

[06:35] Liam: sure. (screen share noise) so, in TS it looks like:
- define function: get_inventory(product_id) -> returns {available: number, warehouse: string}
- call via sdk.chat.callFunction({ name: 'get_inventory', args: {product_id}})
- response: {role: 'tool', name: 'get_inventory', content: '{"available":12, "warehouse":"SJC"}'}

[07:00] Sara: will Redwood auto-run the function or do we have to implement the function runner?

[07:04] Liam: you implement the function runner; Redwood returns the tool call payload. but we do support a local emulator pattern in the SDK so you can wire it up quickly for dev. there's also a helper that will call your function and pass results back into the model loop if you opt-in.

[07:35] Priya: for compliance we need the tool calls to not include user PII. is there a way to redact at the SDK layer?

[07:41] Maya: yes there's a middleware hook in the SDK for request sanitization; we can push a sample sanitizer that strips emails and phone numbers. also we can set tokenization redaction in the Console for logs.

[08:10] Tom: networking  we have strict egress rules and only allow traffic through a proxy. can Redwood work with our proxy for hosted? or do we need Dedicated/Private?

[08:21] Maya: you can reach hosted via proxy but if you want VPC peering and no egress through the public internet, that's Dedicated or Private. we should get your network diagram; Tom mentioned he'll share that.

[08:45] Tom: yes I'll dump the diagram, thanks.

[09:00] Priya: quick question on model variants  for fallback, can we set policy like prefer low-cost quantized model, but route to higher-quality variant on failure?

[09:10] Liam: yep, smart routing supports policy-based routing: cost-first, latency-first, or quality-first. you can also define rollouts; e.g., primary route to quantized model (faster, cheaper) with a canary to higher-quality. we also support an automatic fallback if generation confidence is low.

[09:45] Sara: how do you measure confidence? is that a probability or a heuristic?

[09:50] Liam: it's a heuristic based on log-likelihood and token-level uncertainty; we expose a confidence score in the metadata. pro tip: calibrate it with your prompt set in the benchmark.

[10:15] Maya: ok let's walk through the benchmark plan. we'll run 5k requests derived from your sample prompts  we'll measure latency (p50/p90), token cost, success rate for schema validation, and fallback frequency. we'll return a per-route breakdown for hosted vs dedicated kernels.

[10:45] Priya: for success criteria: we want schema validation >= 98% and avg cost < $0.004, p50 <= 250ms. if we can't get to that we need a clear plan for mitigation (caching, quantization, dedicated).

[11:10] Liam: understood. one caveat: p50 250ms on hosted with cold KV cahce.. might be tough. dedicated with pinned kernels will be more predictable.

[11:45] Tom: what about batch vs streaming? our front-end expects quick single-turn sync responses not streaming.

[11:52] Liam: fine  Redwood supports both; streaming helps with perceived latency but doesn't reduce total compute. for your single-turn attribute extraction, non-streaming is okay and usually simpler for structured output.

[12:20] Priya: can we see an example of structured output schema? we have fields: sku, price_cents, availability_status, attributes[].

[12:28] Liam: we'll include a recommended JSON schema. quick sample in chat: {"sku":"string","price_cents":"integer","availability_status":{"enum":["in_stock","out_of_stock"]},"attributes":[{"name":"string","value":"string"}]}  um note: transcription may remove braces.

[13:00] Speaker 2: (brief) sounds good

[13:10] Sara: on the SDK, is there support for typed responses in TS so we don't have to cast?

[13:14] Liam: yes we provide types generated from the JSON schema in the TS SDK helper  it's beta but we can generate an interface for you as part of the SDK snippet.

[13:50] Priya: security docs  Maya can you confirm SOC2 scope and if we can get a shared responsibility matrix?

[13:59] Maya: yes SOC 2 Type II in scope for hosted; Dedicated + Private have additional controls. we'll share the SR matrix in the security folder and highlight what is Redwood's responsibility vs Acme's.

[14:30] Tom: any PCI / data residency concerns? we operate in EU and US; some catalogs are restricted to EU data centers.

[14:36] Maya: Redwood supports region pinning and we have EU regions. for Private deployment we can do on-prem or VPC with EU-only egress. we'll note this for the POC.

[15:00] Priya: okay, real-time integration question  when the tool call triggers an inventory check, we need deterministic throughput for 200 QPS at peak. can Redwood do that on hosted or do we need Dedicated?

[15:09] Liam: for sustained 200 QPS Dedicated is preferred  you can reserve GPUs and avoid noisy neighbor issues. hosted can sometimes sustain bursts but not guaranteed. Dedicated also helps with consistent latency.

[15:45] Maya: we'll propose two benchmark tracks: hosted baseline and dedicated profile with 1-2 GPU nodes to measure stability at 200 QPS.

[16:10] Speaker 1: (background) yep

[16:25] Priya: about logs  we need per-request logs for debug but with redaction. is that configurable?

[16:31] Liam: yep, logging levels are configurable; you can enable request-level logs and configure redaction rules. logs can be exported to your SIEM.

[16:50] Sara: small nit  when the SDK returns tool call responses, are timestamps UTC? we rely on consistent timezones for audit.

[16:56] Liam: all timestamps are in ISO UTC in the audit logs.

[17:20] Maya: quick demo note  we dropped a sample repo link in the chat: https://redwood.example/poc/acme/sdk-samples (note: placeholder). also benchmark sheet: https://sheets.example/redwood/acme-bench (placeholder).

[17:50] Priya: We'll use those, thanks.

[18:10] Tom: regarding cost  how granular are cost breakdowns? can we see per-route token breakdown and per-request unit costs?

[18:18] Maya: yes, Console gives token-level breakdown, CPU/GPU kernel cost estimates per model variant, and per-request billable tokens. we'll include an export for your account so you can slice by route.

[18:45] Priya: any gotchas with structured output when the model returns arrays with unexpected extra fields? how strict is the validation?

[18:52] Liam: validation is strict by default but you can set a mode: strict vs permissive. in permissive mode we return the best-effort parse and annotate unknown fields in the metadata. strict mode will flag and count as validation failure which triggers fallback if you configured it.

[19:20] Sara: Could you show a quick example where the model returns a slightly different field name and how the SDK handles it?

[19:28] Liam: sure: model outputs "availibility" instead of "availability_status"  in permissive mode the SDK will attempt to map close strings and include a _warnings array. in strict mode it fails validation and returns the raw text plus a parse error.

[20:00] Speaker 3: (typing)

[20:10] Priya: question on canaries/rollouts  if we do a canary to high-quality model, can we split by user cohort?

[20:16] Maya: yes, you can route by user attribute, by percent, or by header. we can show config examples.

[20:45] Tom: ok let's talk timeline. We're aiming to go into a limited pilot by end of May. what are milestones?

[20:53] Maya: milestone proposal: share prompts and infra diagram this week, Redwood runs benchmarks next week and returns results + SDK snippets, then we do a two-week canary in late April / early May, then pilot end of May.

[21:20] Priya: that timeline works if benchmarks are quick. any blockers?

[21:24] Liam: main blocker is full prompt set and network diagram. also, we might need escalation for KMS if your security team requires HSM onsite certs.

[21:45] Sara: I'm going to test the schema validation locally  will the SDK let me run it offline?

[21:50] Liam: yes, the SDK includes an offline validator. it will replicate Redwood's server-side rules for most cases. we do reserve some server-only checks but it's good for dev.

[22:20] Maya: quick recap of technical changes since last week  we fixed a bug in the TypeScript SDK where function-call args were stringified incorrectly; that should be in the snippet Liam will share.

[22:45] Priya: awesome, we saw that fix in the repo. thanks.

[23:05] Liam: I'm going to pastebin the SDK examples right after this call, will include both the TS typed interface, Python sample, and a small local emulator for tool calls.

[23:30] Tom: on the benchmarking metrics, can you provide p50/p90 as well as cold vs warm?

[23:36] Maya: yes, we'll provide cold/warm breakdowns, and also per-model kernel breakdown.

[24:00] Priya: one more question  for logs retention, what's default retention and can we extend?

[24:07] Maya: default retention 30 days for hosted logs, extendable for Dedicated/Private. enterprise retention add-on available.

[24:40] Sara: ok, I'll try the local validator and report back.

[25:00] Liam: quick note  please include edge-case prompts in the sample set (eg weird SKU formatting) so the schema calibration picks them up.

[25:22] Priya: will do.

[25:40] Speaker 2: (murmur)

[26:00] Priya: about the fallback  if validation fails and we fallback to a human in the loop, can Redwood tag the event and route to our internal queue?

[26:09] Liam: yes events have hooks; you can trigger a webhook on validation failure with payload and then route to your internal ticketing.

[26:40] Tom: any limitations on webhooks throughput? at 200 QPS we might generate many events if we do per-request.

[26:47] Maya: webhooks can be batched or sampled; for high QPS we recommend event sampling or a sidecar that consumes the webhook and aggregates. we'll document patterns.

[27:20] Priya: are there any special steps for EU data residency with webhooks? we need them to stay in EU.

[27:27] Liam: we can configure webhook egress regionally, yes.

[27:50] Speaker 1: (phone ringing)

[28:10] Maya: ok  last technical item: quantization. we suggested an 8-bit quantized model for cost savings; any concerns about quality for structured extraction?

[28:18] Sara: we noticed small degradations in earlier tests; need to validate.

[28:25] Liam: quantization sometimes affects open-ended generation more than structured extraction; still, we'll include quantized variants in the benchmark so you can compare.

[28:55] Priya: good.

[29:10] Maya: recapping next steps (live): 1) Acme sends prompts + infra diagram, 2) Redwood runs the 5k benchmark and returns results, 3) Redwood shares SDK samples + sanitizer + schema generator, 4) schedule canary test.

[29:35] Priya: confirmed.

[30:00] Tom: small ops question  how do we rotate API keys without downtime?

[30:06] Liam: we support key rotation with overlap window; create a new key, deploy, then retire the old key. for Dedicated we can rotate via your KMS as well.

[30:30] Sara: happy with that.

[31:00] Priya: anything else on compliance?

[31:05] Maya: we'll attach a redacted SOC2 report and an SR matrix after the call.

[31:28] Speaker 2: (agree)

[32:00] Maya: ok we're at about half time, want to open for any deep dive items?

[32:08] Tom: maybe a quick deep dive on the SDK's retry/backoff logic for network errors.

[32:13] Liam: sure  SDK has exponential backoff with jitter, configurable max retries, and idempotency token support so you can safely retry function calls.

[32:45] Sara: will that preserve order if we're doing multi-step flows?

[32:49] Liam: order preservation is on the client; we provide idempotency and sequence tokens to help. for strict ordering you'd probably want to serialize on your side or use the session KV.

[33:15] Priya: ok great.

[33:40] Maya: quick check  any open blockers from Acme side?

[33:44] Priya: main blocker is internal security review for KMS integration  I need to get the security team sign-off.

[34:00] Tom: plus we need to confirm network egress rules with NetOps.

[34:10] Maya: understood. we'll liaise with your security and NetOps if helpful.

[34:30] Priya: one more ask  can Redwood provide a short decision matrix for hosted vs dedicated that we can share with our leadership?

[34:37] Maya: yes, we'll send a one-pager: tradeoffs, expected latency/cost buckets, and recommended POC path.

[35:00] Speaker 3: (typing)

[35:25] Liam: I'm going to call out a small thing: when you pass JSON schema with required fields, try to make fields optional where appropriate to reduce brittle failures.

[35:40] Sara: noted.

[36:00] Priya: okay, any questions about the function calling emulator?

[36:06] Liam: emulator runs as a local node process, intercepts tool calls and either returns preset fixture or runs your actual function depending on config. dev-friendly.

[36:35] Tom: will you include Docker compose for the emulator?

[36:38] Liam: yes snippet will include a docker-compose service.

[37:00] Maya: good. I'm going to read back the main next steps so we all align.

[37:05] Maya: Redwood items: run benchmark (5k), SDK samples (TS+Py), security docs, one-pager decision matrix. Acme items: send prompts, infra diagram, run local validator and give feedback.

[37:20] Priya: that's accurate.

[37:40] Speaker 1: (quiet)

[38:00] Tom: about costs  if we go Dedicated, what's the minimum commit?

[38:07] Maya: typical committed plans start at a monthly baseline  we'll propose a right-sized starting config after the benchmark; there's flex for startups vs enterprise.

[38:30] Priya: will that include support SLAs?

[38:34] Maya: yes support tier is separate but can be bundled. we'll provide pricing options.

[39:00] Sara: on logs export  can we forward to our S3 in EU?

[39:06] Liam: yes logs can be exported to customer S3 with region restrictions for Private/Dedicated; hosted may require a connector. we'll detail options.

[39:35] Priya: ok I think we're in good shape.

[40:00] Maya: any final technical clarifications?

[40:06] Sara: none from me.

[40:15] Tom: none.

[40:20] Priya: quick ask  can Redwood include an example of schema migration when fields are added? we want a graceful upgrade pattern.

[40:28] Liam: yes  we'll include a migration example: add new field as optional, then run a revalidation job to find failures, then flip to required once coverage is good.

[40:55] Maya: Perfect. wrapping up, we'll share links to artifacts and action items within 24-48 hours.

[41:10] Priya: thanks all.

[41:15] Maya: Thanks  we'll follow up after the benchmark.

[41:30] End of recording (approx 58 minutes).

Notes / Artifacts referenced:
- SDK samples (TS + Python) link: https://redwood.example/poc/acme/sdk-samples (placeholder)
- Benchmark spreadsheet: https://sheets.example/redwood/acme-bench (placeholder)
